axes: Roblox (x, y, z) = Blender (x, z, -y); an asset's front is Roblox -Z (LookVector)

files.Creatures.glb: one MeshPart per colour: use each part's rgb and robloxMaterial (list 'parts'). No vertex colours, no textures, no UVs.
files.Creatures_VC.glb: one MeshPart per moving piece (list 'partsVC'), colours in COLOR_0. vertexColors 'full' = the mesh carries its colours, set MeshPart.Color to rgb (white); 'shade' = the mesh carries a light/dark multiplier only, set MeshPart.Color to rgb (the part's colour, tintable). If the colours do not arrive in Studio, use the flat file, or set fallbackRgb.

vertexColourSpace: linear floats in the file, as the glTF spec says; the intended sRGB values are in 'palette'. If Studio shows them too dark, re-run with CREATURES_VC_SRGB=1.
import: Assets sit in a row along X; 'origin' is each asset's pivot in the file. Part 'center' and 'size' are relative to that pivot (Roblox space), because the importer puts a MeshPart's position at its bounding box centre.
Everything is visual: CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch off except the CookFire parts marked collide. Squirrels get one invisible hitbox (see 'hitbox').
No part is double-sided: wings carry real back faces (the slate underside).

assets.name: SquirrelSit
assets.notes: Sitting up on its haunches, forepaws at the chest, tail in an S behind. Origin on the ground under the body; faces Roblox -Z.

hitbox.note: mesh parts are CanQuery off; weld one invisible box this size for arrows, thrown knives and the pick-up prompt

assets.name: SquirrelRun
assets.notes: Stretched mid-bound, tail streaming. Origin on the ground under the body centre; faces Roblox -Z. The paws are a little off the ground on purpose (it is in the air).

hitbox.note: mesh parts are CanQuery off; weld one invisible box this size for arrows, thrown knives and the pick-up prompt

assets.name: SquirrelClimb
assets.notes: Clinging head-up to a trunk. Origin = the point on the bark under the belly; LookVector (Roblox -Z) points INTO the trunk and Roblox +Y is up the trunk, so place it with CFrame.lookAt(barkPoint, barkPoint - surfaceNormal). Turn it about its LookVector for head-down.

hitbox.note: mesh parts are CanQuery off; weld one invisible box this size for arrows, thrown knives and the pick-up prompt

assets.name: SquirrelStill
assets.notes: Lying on its side with closed eyes (asleep-looking, no wound). Origin on the ground under the body; the head points to Roblox -Z, the legs to Roblox -X.

hitbox.note: mesh parts are CanQuery off; weld one invisible box this size for arrows, thrown knives and the pick-up prompt

assets.name: SquirrelSpit
assets.notes: The turning stick with a trussed roast (no head, no face). Origin on the stick axis at its middle; the stick runs along Roblox X. Put the origin on CookFire.SpitAxis and spin it about its own X axis. SquirrelSpit_Meat is one flat colour: tint it raw -> cooked -> burnt (palette in the manifest), or hide it to show the bare stick.

spin.note: rotate the whole asset about its own Roblox X axis

assets.name: cooked_meat
assets.notes: A roasted haunch on the bone, held by the bone. Same contract as Items.glb: origin = hand grip, item axis = Roblox +Y, Grip look = +Y, up = -Z. cooked_meat_Meat is one flat colour (tint raw/cooked/burnt).

assets.name: CookFire
assets.notes: A small cooking fire: stone ring 3.5 across, ash bed, five logs, an ember bed (Neon) and two forked uprights for the spit. Origin = ground centre of the ring; the spit runs along Roblox X. The Frame part can be hidden when there is no spit. Add the fire, light and sound at FireCenter. Stones are low enough to step over; a 5.5-stud character crouches at CrouchSpot_1/2 with the roast at chest height.
assets.pivot: ground centre of the stone ring

assets.name: Butterfly
assets.notes: Blue stinging butterfly, wings exported FLAT (lift 0). Origin = the thorax, on the hinge line; faces Roblox -Z. Each wing turns about its hinge, a line along the body (Roblox Z axis) through HingeL / HingeR: lift a (radians) = WingR * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, +a), WingL * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, -a), applied about the hinge point. Flap between about -25 and +78 degrees; 84 degrees is fully closed. The top is vivid blue with a dark edge, the underside slate with one pale eye, so a flapping wing flashes. The sting, antenna tips and eyes are the pale charge colour.
assets.pivot: thorax centre on the hinge line

flap.formula: wing.CFrame = body.CFrame * CFrame.new(hinge) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, sign * a) * CFrame.new(-hinge) * wingOffsetAtExport; sign = +1 for WingR, -1 for WingL

assets.name: ButterflyRest
assets.notes: The same butterfly at rest: wings closed over its back (lift 84 degrees), showing the slate underside and its pale eye. A static model; origin = under the body (where it stands on a leaf or twig); faces Roblox -Z.

assets.name: ButterflyFar
assets.notes: A 14-triangle stand-in for swarm members far from the camera: two plain wings raised 30 degrees and a body, one part in the vertex-colour file. Same origin and facing as Butterfly. To fake a flap, scale the part's X size up and down.

notes: One upload per file through Open Cloud POST /assets/v1/assets (creator user 5458010221), 18 Nov 2026, approved by the owner ("Yes, upload them"). Never re-upload this file; reuse its id. A re-export needs a new upload (new id) recorded here.
No textures, no vertex colours: one flat colour per part; the importer drops colours, so set Material/Color from this manifest. Not inserted into the place (an upload check only).
